A developer’s approach.
A practical problem.

Does the invoice match what was agreed and delivered?

That question is the starting point for Margevia. For restaurant groups and caterers, answering it can mean moving between supplier price lists, delivery notes and invoices, then keeping track of the follow-up.

Adham is building a clearer way to do that work. Margevia brings the comparison and its supporting evidence into one review workflow, so purchasing, operations and finance teams can understand a difference before deciding what to do.

His full-stack development background connects the product idea to its implementation. He leads the build, from the interface people use to the document-processing workflows being explored next.

Building. Testing.
Listening.

Three pilot users. A working preview. The next questions are practical.

Adham has launched Margevia’s website and interactive demo, and built the pilot enquiry flow. His focus now is validating the workflow with real purchasing documents and learning from user feedback.

AI-assisted extraction and matching are being evaluated. The public demo uses fictional records; live document processing and accounting integrations are still in development.
